title: Property (T) above one-third density in random free-product quotients
description:
Fix at least three nontrivial finitely generated groups, a finite nonempty inverse-closed generating alphabet of nonidentity elements in each factor, and a density 1/3 less than d less than 1. For the quotient by floor(|S_l|^d) independent uniform rooted cyclically reduced syllable relators of exact length l, sampled with replacement, the probability of Kazhdan property (T) tends to one through all integer lengths. This gives an affirmative resolution of the at-least-three-factor property-(T) question in Problem 16 of the 2026 Oberwolfach report Median Geometry and Applications. Fixed-radius word-ball alphabets with integer radius at least one are included. The theorem does not settle the broader two-factor Question 1.9 of Random Quotients of Free Products, the critical density 1/3, or varying-parameter uniformity. Known collapse already gives property (T) above 1/2; the substantive extension includes every density in (1/3,1/2].

The proof completes model-specific steps of an established spectral program. Montee and Steenbock already proposed the syllable-respecting three-part strategy in their project report in ESI Annual Report 2024, pp.77-79, especially p.78; that volume is copyright 2025 with an August 2025 preface. Ashcroft already treats all integer lengths with almost-equal blocks in the ordinary free-group model, and Drutu-Mackay supply the common-suffix finite-index precedent. The present argument supplies the exact weighted endpoint kernel, torsion-compatible inverse-fixed-block deletion and suffix choices, unequal-length type-matrix spectrum, and concentration of independent whole-relator Laplacians. It uses established Ballmann-Swiatkowski-Zuk/Kotowski-Kotowski and Tropp results. No invention of the general strategy, new spectral criterion, verified firstness, exhaustive novelty, or worldwide current-open-status certificate is claimed.

The deposit contains a seven-page research note and a verification archive with editable source, all 15 frozen original files, three original evidence archives with 26 members, independent analytical and bounded priority audit evidence, primary-source version/hash locators, an externally pinned closed-inventory verifier, safe optional source reads, isolated relocated finite-diagnostic replay, and a deterministic ZIP builder. Default replay checks 14 exact positive/negative diagnostic receipts; optional provenance replay checks 20 receipts when the three pinned corpora and six pinned PDFs are supplied separately. Downloaded publications, source extracts, page renders, raw corpora and private credentials are excluded. Finite checks authenticate artifacts and test formulas; they do not certify the asymptotic theorem or priority. Byte reproducibility is bounded to identical inputs and the same Python ZIP implementation and zlib.

OpenAI tools were used extensively in solving, proof development, drafting, coding and adversarial verification. This is an unrefereed preprint; no completed external human peer review or formal proof-assistant verification is claimed. The mathematical argument assumes the explicitly identified established spectral, concentration, normal-form and finite-dimensional linear-algebra results.
